title: Earliest writing at Uruk
summary: Proto-cuneiform tablets from the Eanna precinct record temple accounts — the oldest known writing system.

sources.cite: Uruk IV–III tablets, Eanna precinct (German excavations)

title: Narmer unites Upper and Lower Egypt
summary: The first dynasty of pharaohs rules a single Egyptian state from the Nile Delta to the First Cataract.

title: Steppe migration into Europe
summary: Ancient DNA shows people with Yamnaya-related ancestry moving into central and northern Europe, forming the Corded Ware culture.

title: Indus cities at their height
summary: The Mature Harappan phase begins: planned cities such as Mohenjo-daro and Harappa share standard bricks, weights and seals.

sources.cite: J. Marshall, Mohenjo-daro and the Indus Civilization (1931)

title: Caral's pyramids rise in Peru
summary: Monumental platform mounds at Caral make it one of the oldest cities in the Americas.

title: Great Pyramid of Khufu built
summary: Logbooks of an inspector named Merer record hauling limestone blocks to Giza for Khufu's pyramid.

sources.cite: Wadi al-Jarf papyri ('Diary of Merer'), found 2013

title: Sargon founds the Akkadian Empire
summary: Sargon of Akkad conquers the Sumerian city-states and campaigns to the Mediterranean. The location of his capital, Akkad, is unknown, so this marker is approximate.

sources.cite: Sargon's inscriptions, Old Babylonian copies from Nippur (RIME 2)

title: Ur-Nammu founds the Third Dynasty of Ur
summary: A last Sumerian empire rises at Ur, building the great ziggurat and issuing the oldest surviving law code.

sources.cite: Code of Ur-Nammu (tablets from Nippur and Ur)
Ziggurat of Ur, excavated by C. L. Woolley

title: Elamites sack Ur
summary: Elamite armies capture Ur and carry off its last king, Ibbi-Sin, ending Sumerian political dominance.

title: Code of Hammurabi
summary: Having unified Mesopotamia, Hammurabi of Babylon publishes 282 laws on a basalt stele.

sources.cite: Stele of Hammurabi (Louvre Sb 8), found at Susa 1901

title: Hittite Old Kingdom at Hattusa
summary: Hattusili I rules from Hattusa and campaigns into Syria, founding the Hittite kingdom.

title: Shang dynasty established
summary: Tradition dates the Shang to c. 1600 BC; its early capital is often identified with the walled site at Zhengzhou.

title: Hittites sack Babylon
summary: Mursili I raids deep into Mesopotamia and ends Hammurabi's dynasty (date by the middle chronology).

title: Egypt destroys Kerma
summary: New Kingdom armies under Thutmose I sack the Nubian capital and push the frontier to the Fourth Cataract.

title: Battle of Megiddo
summary: Thutmose III defeats a Canaanite coalition — the first battle recorded in detail — opening Egypt's Levantine empire.

sources.cite: Annals of Thutmose III, Temple of Karnak

title: Akhenaten founds Amarna
summary: A new capital for the sun-disc Aten. Its archive of diplomatic letters links Egypt, Babylon, Mitanni, Assyria and the Hittites.

title: Suppiluliuma I breaks Mitanni
summary: The Hittite king sacks Washukanni and installs a vassal, ending Mitanni as a great power.

sources.cite: Treaty of Suppiluliuma I and Shattiwaza (CTH 51)

title: Hittite treaty with Alaksandu of Wilusa
summary: Muwatalli II binds Alaksandu, king of Wilusa — widely identified with Troy (Ilios) — as a Hittite vassal.

title: Battle of Kadesh
summary: Ramesses II and Muwatalli II clash in Syria in perhaps the largest chariot battle ever fought. Both sides claimed victory.

sources.cite: Kadesh 'Poem' and 'Bulletin' at Abu Simbel, Karnak, Luxor and the Ramesseum

title: Egyptian–Hittite peace treaty
summary: Ramesses II and Hattusili III sign the earliest peace treaty whose text survives on both sides.

sources.cite: Hittite clay tablet from Hattusa (Istanbul Archaeology Museums)
Egyptian hieroglyphic version, Karnak and Ramesseum

title: Merneptah Stele names 'Israel'
summary: An Egyptian victory hymn lists 'Israel' among peoples of Canaan, the earliest mention of the name outside the Bible.

sources.cite: Merneptah Stele (Egyptian Museum, Cairo JE 31408), found by Petrie 1896

title: Hattusa abandoned
summary: The Hittite capital is emptied and partly burned during the Late Bronze Age collapse. The kingdom does not recover.

title: Destruction of Troy VIIa
summary: The citadel at Hisarlık is destroyed by fire, with signs of warfare. It is the leading archaeological candidate for Homer's Troy.

title: Ramesses III fights the Sea Peoples
summary: Egypt repels a migrating coalition by land and sea in the Nile Delta, as states across the eastern Mediterranean collapse.

sources.cite: Medinet Habu inscriptions and reliefs, Year 8 of Ramesses III

title: Battle of Muye
summary: King Wu of Zhou defeats the last Shang king, founding the Zhou dynasty and the 'Mandate of Heaven' doctrine.

title: Shoshenq I (Shishak) invades Judah and Israel
summary: 1 Kings 14:25 says Shishak came against Jerusalem in Rehoboam's fifth year; Shoshenq I's own relief at Karnak lists conquered towns of the region.

sources.cite: Bubastite Portal relief of Shoshenq I, Karnak

title: Battle of Qarqar
summary: A coalition including Ahab of Israel, who brought 2,000 chariots, and Hadadezer of Damascus confronts Shalmaneser III in Syria.

sources.cite: Kurkh Monolith of Shalmaneser III (British Museum)

title: Jehu pays tribute to Assyria
summary: The Black Obelisk shows Jehu of Israel, or his envoy, bowing before Shalmaneser III: the only surviving image of an Israelite king.

title: Tel Dan and Mesha steles
summary: Aramean and Moabite victory inscriptions name the kings of Israel and the 'House of David', the earliest outside references.

title: Carthage founded
summary: Phoenician settlers from Tyre found Carthage. The traditional date comes from the historian Timaeus; radiocarbon dates from the earliest layers are close.

sources.cite: Timaeus of Tauromenium, via Dionysius of Halicarnassus, Roman Antiquities 1.74
Early Carthage radiocarbon studies (Docter et al., 2005)

title: First recorded Olympic Games
summary: The base date of Greek Olympiad chronology, from a victor list compiled by Hippias of Elis.

sources.cite: Hippias of Elis's Olympic victor list, via Eusebius, Chronicle

title: Traditional founding of Rome
summary: Romulus founds the city, according to the date calculated by Varro. Huts on the Palatine Hill date to roughly this period.

sources.cite: Iron Age huts on the Palatine (A. Carandini's excavations)

title: Assyria conquers Damascus
summary: Tiglath-pileser III takes Damascus and annexes Galilee and Gilead, answering Ahaz of Judah's appeal (2 Kings 16).

title: Piye of Kush conquers Egypt
summary: The Kushite king sails north and takes Memphis, founding Egypt's 25th Dynasty.

title: Assyria destroys the Kingdom of Israel
summary: Samaria falls, and Sargon II claims to have deported 27,290 inhabitants.

title: Sennacherib besieges Lachish
summary: Sennacherib's campaign against Judah is known from Assyrian annals, palace reliefs, the Hebrew Bible and the excavated siege ramp.

sources.cite: Lachish reliefs (British Museum); Assyrian siege ramp at Tel Lachish

title: Hezekiah's Tunnel
summary: A 533-metre tunnel brings the Gihon spring inside Jerusalem's walls before Sennacherib's invasion; its workers carved an inscription at the meeting point.

sources.cite: Siloam inscription, written by the tunnellers (Istanbul Archaeology Museums)

title: Ashurbanipal sacks Susa
summary: Assyria devastates the Elamite capital, desecrating royal tombs.

title: Fall of Nineveh
summary: Babylonians and Medes storm the Assyrian capital. The empire is extinguished by 609 BC.

title: Nebuchadnezzar takes Jerusalem
summary: Babylon captures the city on 16 March 597 BC and deports King Jehoiachin; ration tablets from Babylon later list 'Jehoiachin, king of Judah'.

title: Babylonian siege of Lachish
summary: A Judahite officer writes to his commander that he can no longer see the signal fires of Azekah, echoing Jeremiah 34:7.

title: Babylon destroys Jerusalem
summary: Nebuchadnezzar II destroys the First Temple and deports Judah's elite to Babylon.

sources.cite: Babylonian Chronicle ABC 5 (for the 597 BC capture)

title: Cyrus defeats the Medes
summary: Astyages' army mutinies and Cyrus of Anshan takes the Median capital, Ecbatana, founding the Persian Empire.

title: Cyrus conquers Lydia
summary: Croesus is defeated and Sardis taken, bringing the Greek cities of Ionia under Persian rule.

title: Cyrus takes Babylon
summary: Babylon falls almost without a fight. Cyrus presents himself as restorer of the city's gods.

title: Cyrus permits the return from exile
summary: Exiles return to Jerusalem to rebuild the Temple. The Cyrus Cylinder records a similar policy of restoring deported peoples and their gods.

title: Darius I carves the Behistun Inscription
summary: A trilingual rock inscription justifying Darius's seizure of the throne. Its decipherment unlocked cuneiform.

title: Second Temple completed
summary: The rebuilt Temple is dedicated in the sixth year of Darius I.

title: Roman Republic founded
summary: Romans expel King Tarquinius Superbus and elect two consuls annually.

title: Battle of Marathon
summary: Athens and Plataea defeat a Persian expeditionary force sent by Darius I.

sources.cite: Soros burial mound of the Athenian dead

title: Thermopylae and Salamis
summary: Xerxes forces the pass at Thermopylae and burns Athens, but the Greek fleet destroys the Persian navy at Salamis.

sources.cite: Aeschylus, The Persians (472 BC, by a veteran)

title: Nehemiah rebuilds Jerusalem's walls
summary: Artaxerxes I's cupbearer rebuilds the walls in 52 days, opposed by Sanballat of Samaria, who also appears in the Elephantine papyri.

title: Peloponnesian War begins
summary: Athens and Sparta begin a 27-year war that ends Athens' empire in 404 BC.

sources.cite: Thucydides, History of the Peloponnesian War

title: Siege of Tyre
summary: Alexander builds a causeway to the island city and takes it after seven months.

title: Battle of Gaugamela
summary: Alexander defeats Darius III decisively, and Babylon, Susa and Persepolis fall within months.

title: Death of Alexander at Babylon
summary: Alexander dies at 32. His generals' wars of succession carve up the empire.

title: Chandragupta founds the Maurya Empire
summary: Chandragupta overthrows the Nanda dynasty of Magadha and expands to the Indus.

title: Seleucus retakes Babylon
summary: This starts the Seleucid Era, the first continuous year count, used in the Near East for over a thousand years.

title: Ptolemy I proclaims himself king of Egypt
summary: Alexander's general takes the royal title, founding the dynasty that would end with Cleopatra.

title: Ashoka's Kalinga War
summary: The conquest kills, by Ashoka's own account, 100,000 people. His remorse leads him to promote dhamma.

title: Qin unifies China
summary: Having conquered the last Warring State, King Zheng takes the title Shi Huangdi, 'First Emperor'.

title: Battle of Cannae
summary: Hannibal encircles and destroys a Roman army of about 80,000 in southern Italy.

title: Liu Bang founds the Han dynasty
summary: After the Qin collapse, Liu Bang defeats his rival Xiang Yu and becomes Emperor Gaozu.

title: Battle of Zama
summary: Scipio defeats Hannibal in Africa, ending the Second Punic War and Carthage's empire.

title: Memphis Decree (Rosetta Stone)
summary: A priestly decree honouring Ptolemy V, in hieroglyphic, Demotic and Greek. In 1822 it enabled Champollion to decipher hieroglyphs.

title: Battle of Magnesia
summary: Rome defeats Antiochus III. The Treaty of Apamea strips the Seleucids of Anatolia.

title: Maccabean revolt
summary: Antiochus IV outlaws Jewish practice and desecrates the Temple; the priest Mattathias and his sons revolt. Judas rededicates the Temple in 164 BC (Hanukkah).

title: Rome destroys Carthage and Corinth
summary: At the end of the Third Punic War Carthage is razed. The same year Corinth is sacked and Greece falls under Roman control.

sources.cite: Polybius 38–39 (fragments; he was an eyewitness at Carthage)

title: Parthians take Seleucia
summary: Mithridates I conquers Mesopotamia, confining the Seleucids to Syria.

title: Attalus III bequeaths Pergamon to Rome
summary: The last Attalid king wills his kingdom to Rome, which makes it the province of Asia.

title: Pompey takes Jerusalem
summary: Pompey storms the Temple Mount and enters the Holy of Holies; Judea becomes a Roman client state.

title: Battle of Carrhae
summary: Parthian horse archers annihilate Crassus' legions, and Crassus is killed.

title: Herod takes Jerusalem
summary: With Roman legions, Herod captures Jerusalem from the last Hasmonean king, Antigonus.

title: Battle of Actium
summary: Octavian's fleet defeats Antony and Cleopatra. Egypt is annexed the next year, ending the Ptolemaic kingdom.

title: Octavian becomes Augustus
summary: The Senate grants Octavian the name Augustus, conventionally marking the start of the Roman Empire.

title: Death of Herod the Great
summary: Herod dies at Jericho; Augustus divides his kingdom among his sons Archelaus, Antipas and Philip.

title: Battle of the Teutoburg Forest
summary: Arminius' Germanic coalition destroys three legions under Varus. Rome abandons conquest east of the Rhine.

title: Crucifixion of Jesus
summary: Jesus of Nazareth is executed in Jerusalem under the prefect Pontius Pilate, probably in AD 30 or 33. His followers proclaim his resurrection, and Christianity spreads across the empire.

sources.cite: Gospels of Matthew, Mark, Luke and John

title: Paul in Corinth
summary: Paul stays 18 months in Corinth and is brought before the proconsul Gallio (Acts 18:12), whose term is dated by an inscription at Delphi.

title: Great Fire of Rome and Nero's persecution
summary: Fire destroys much of Rome; Nero blames the Christians, the first recorded Roman persecution.

title: Destruction of the Second Temple
summary: Titus captures Jerusalem after a five-month siege and the Temple burns, ending the Great Jewish Revolt's main phase.

sources.cite: Arch of Titus, Rome; burnt house, Jerusalem

title: Fall of Masada
summary: The last rebel fortress falls to a Roman siege ramp; Josephus says its defenders chose death over capture.

title: Vesuvius buries Pompeii
summary: The eruption preserves two Roman towns, a frozen picture of everyday life.

title: Trajan conquers Dacia
summary: Sarmizegetusa falls and Decebalus kills himself. Rome's new province is rich in gold.

title: Rome annexes the Nabataean kingdom
summary: The province of Arabia Petraea is created after the death of the last Nabataean king.

title: Roman Empire at its greatest extent
summary: Trajan's conquests reach the Persian Gulf. Hadrian gives up Mesopotamia shortly after.

title: Kanishka becomes Kushan emperor
summary: The greatest Kushan ruler begins a new era; his reign is dated by the Rabatak inscription.

title: Bar Kokhba revolt
summary: A second Jewish revolt (132–135) is crushed by Hadrian, who refounds Jerusalem as Aelia Capitolina.

sources.cite: Bar Kokhba letters, Cave of Letters (found 1960–61)

title: End of the Han dynasty
summary: Emperor Xian abdicates to Cao Pi, beginning the Three Kingdoms period.

sources.cite: Chen Shou, Records of the Three Kingdoms (Sanguozhi)

title: Ardashir overthrows the Parthians
summary: Ardashir I defeats Artabanus IV and founds the Sasanian Empire.

sources.cite: Rock reliefs at Firuzabad and Naqsh-e Rostam
al-Tabari, History of Prophets and Kings

title: Shapur I captures Emperor Valerian
summary: Near Edessa a Roman emperor is taken prisoner for the first and only time.

sources.cite: Shapur I's inscription at the Ka'ba-ye Zartosht (ŠKZ)
Triumph relief of Shapur I, Naqsh-e Rostam

title: Battle of the Milvian Bridge
summary: Constantine defeats Maxentius outside Rome, reportedly after a vision of the Christian sign.

sources.cite: Lactantius, On the Deaths of the Persecutors 44

title: Edict of Milan
summary: Constantine and Licinius grant religious toleration, ending the persecution of Christians.

sources.cite: Lactantius, On the Deaths of the Persecutors 48

title: Chandragupta I founds the Gupta Empire
summary: The start of the Gupta era. His son Samudragupta's conquests are listed on the Allahabad pillar.

title: First Council of Nicaea
summary: Constantine convenes the bishops to settle the Arian controversy; the council issues the Nicene Creed.

title: Constantinople dedicated
summary: Constantine refounds Byzantium as a new Rome. It would be capital of the Eastern Empire for 1,100 years.

title: Ezana of Aksum adopts Christianity
summary: Aksum's coinage switches from pagan symbols to the cross, making it one of the first Christian states.

title: Julian dies on campaign in Persia
summary: The last pagan emperor is killed retreating from Ctesiphon; Jovian cedes Nisibis to Shapur II.

title: Battle of Adrianople
summary: Gothic refugees fleeing the Huns destroy the eastern Roman field army and kill Emperor Valens.

title: Teotihuacan 'arrival' at Tikal
summary: A Teotihuacan general, Siyaj K'ak', arrives and a new dynasty takes power at Tikal.

title: Roman Empire permanently divided
summary: On Theodosius I's death his sons Arcadius and Honorius rule the East and West separately.

sources.note: Lists the separate eastern and western administrations.

title: Vandals, Alans and Suebi cross the Rhine
summary: On the last day of 406 (traditional date) a migrant coalition breaks into Gaul, near Mainz.

title: Visigoths sack Rome
summary: Alaric's army plunders Rome for three days, the first time in 800 years that the city falls to a foreign enemy.

sources.cite: Orosius, Seven Books of History Against the Pagans 7.39

title: Theodosian Walls built
summary: A triple land wall is completed across the peninsula of Constantinople. It would hold for a thousand years.

title: Vandals seize Carthage
summary: Gaiseric takes Rome's richest African city and its fleet, founding the Vandal Kingdom.

sources.cite: Victor of Vita, History of the Vandal Persecution 1.12

title: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains
summary: Aetius' Romans and Theodoric's Visigoths halt Attila's invasion of Gaul.

title: Council of Chalcedon
summary: Defines Christ as one person in two natures; its rejection by many in Egypt and Syria divides the eastern churches for good.

sources.cite: Acts of the Council of Chalcedon

title: Death of Attila
summary: Attila dies on his wedding night. His sons' quarrels and the Gepid revolt at Nedao (454) break up the Hunnic realm.

title: Vandals sack Rome
summary: Gaiseric's fleet plunders Rome for two weeks and carries off the empress and treasure, including spoils from Jerusalem's Temple.

title: Odoacer deposes the last western emperor
summary: Romulus Augustulus is retired at Ravenna, and Odoacer sends the imperial regalia to Constantinople. The Western Empire ends.

title: Theodoric founds the Ostrogothic Kingdom
summary: Sent by Zeno against Odoacer, Theodoric takes Ravenna and rules Italy in nominal loyalty to Constantinople.

title: Baptism of Clovis
summary: The Frankish king accepts Catholic baptism at Reims, binding the Franks to the Roman church. The date is debated (496–508).

sources.cite: Letter of Avitus of Vienne to Clovis

title: Justinian's Code issued
summary: The first edition of the Codex Justinianus; with the Digest (533) and Institutes it becomes the basis of later European civil law.

title: Battle of Dara
summary: Belisarius wins his first great victory, defeating a larger Persian army in Mesopotamia.

title: Nika riots
summary: Circus factions rise against Justinian and burn much of Constantinople; Belisarius and Mundus massacre the crowd in the Hippodrome.

title: Belisarius destroys the Vandal Kingdom
summary: Victories at Ad Decimum and Tricamarum return Africa to Roman rule. The last Vandal king, Gelimer, surrenders in 534.

title: Gothic War begins
summary: Belisarius invades Sicily and Italy. The war drags on for almost twenty years and devastates the peninsula.

title: Hagia Sophia completed
summary: Justinian's cathedral, built in under six years, holds the record for the world's largest dome for nearly a thousand years.

sources.cite: Paul the Silentiary, Description of Hagia Sophia (563)

title: Belisarius takes Ravenna
summary: The Ostrogothic capital surrenders. The same year Khosrow I sacks Antioch in the east.

title: Khosrow I sacks Antioch
summary: The Persian king breaks the 'Eternal Peace', plunders Antioch and deports its people to a new city near Ctesiphon.

title: Plague of Justinian
summary: Bubonic plague spreads from Egypt to Constantinople in 542, killing a large share of the population in recurring waves.

sources.cite: Yersinia pestis DNA from 6th-c. burials (Wagner et al., 2014)

title: Battle of Taginae (Busta Gallorum)
summary: Narses defeats and kills the Gothic king Totila, effectively ending the Gothic War.

title: Göktürk Khaganate founded
summary: Bumin overthrows the Rouran and founds the first Turkic empire.

title: Lombards invade Italy
summary: Alboin's Lombards cross the Julian Alps; within a few years most of inland Italy is lost to Byzantium.

sources.cite: Paul the Deacon, History of the Lombards 2.7–9

title: Avars take Sirmium
summary: After a long blockade the key Danube city falls, opening the Balkans to Avar and Slav raids.

title: Sui reunifies China
summary: The capture of Jiankang (Nanjing) ends nearly four centuries of division.

title: Maurice restores Khosrow II
summary: Byzantine troops put the exiled Persian prince back on his throne; Persia cedes much of Armenia in return.

title: Phocas overthrows Maurice
summary: The Danube army mutinies; Maurice and his sons are executed. Khosrow II uses the murder as a pretext for war.

title: Heraclius seizes the throne
summary: Sailing from Carthage, Heraclius overthrows Phocas as Persian armies pour into the eastern provinces.

title: Persians capture Jerusalem
summary: Shahrbaraz takes Jerusalem and carries off the relic of the True Cross.

title: Tang dynasty founded
summary: Li Yuan takes power as the Sui collapses and becomes Emperor Gaozu of Tang.

sources.cite: Old Book of Tang (Jiu Tangshu), ch. 1

title: Songtsen Gampo unifies Tibet
summary: The king creates the Tibetan Empire and a written script based on Indian models.

title: Persians conquer Egypt
summary: Alexandria falls, cutting Constantinople off from its grain supply.

title: The Hijra to Medina
summary: Muhammad and his followers move from Mecca to Yathrib (Medina), founding the first Muslim community-state. Year 1 of the Islamic calendar.

sources.cite: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (via Ibn Hisham, 9th c.)
Constitution of Medina (preserved by Ibn Ishaq)

title: Sutton Hoo ship burial
summary: An East Anglian king, probably Rædwald, is buried in a 27-metre ship with treasures from Byzantium to Scandinavia.

title: Avar–Persian siege of Constantinople
summary: With Heraclius away in the Caucasus, the city beats off an Avar-Slav assault while a Persian army waits across the Bosporus.

sources.cite: Theodore Synkellos, homily on the siege

title: Battle of Nineveh
summary: Heraclius destroys a Persian army; Khosrow II is overthrown and killed the next year, and the True Cross is returned.

title: Battle of the Yarmuk
summary: Arab Muslim armies defeat Heraclius' forces. Syria and Palestine are lost to Byzantium.

title: Arabs conquer Egypt
summary: Amr ibn al-As takes Babylon fortress and then Alexandria by treaty, ending nearly seven centuries of Roman rule in Egypt.

title: Death of Yazdegerd III
summary: The last Sasanian shah is killed near Merv while fleeing the Arab conquest.

sources.cite: al-Tabari, History of Prophets and Kings

title: The Baqt treaty with Makuria
summary: After Nubian archers repel an Arab attack on Dongola, a trade-and-truce agreement lasts some 600 years.

title: Battle of the Masts
summary: The new Arab navy defeats Constans II off Lycia, ending Byzantine naval supremacy.

title: Mu'awiya founds the Umayyad Caliphate
summary: After the first civil war, the governor of Syria rules as caliph from Damascus and founds a hereditary dynasty.

sources.cite: al-Tabari, History of Prophets and Kings

title: Constans II moves west to Syracuse
summary: The emperor visits Rome and settles in Sicily, where he is murdered in his bath in 668.

title: Arab siege of Constantinople and Greek fire
summary: Repeated Umayyad attacks (c. 674–678) are repulsed, helped by 'Greek fire', newly invented by Kallinikos.

title: Bulgars defeat Constantine IV
summary: Asparukh's Bulgars rout a Byzantine army in the Danube delta; the peace of 681 recognizes the Bulgar state.

title: Sixth Ecumenical Council
summary: Condemns Monothelitism, the compromise doctrine promoted under Heraclius.

sources.cite: Acts of the Third Council of Constantinople

title: Dome of the Rock completed
summary: Built by Abd al-Malik, it is the oldest surviving major Islamic monument. Its mosaic inscription is dated AH 72.

sources.cite: Dedicatory inscription, Dome of the Rock (AH 72)

title: Arabs take Carthage
summary: The fall of Carthage ends Byzantine Africa. The Arabs found Tunis nearby.

title: Justinian II returns with Bulgar help
summary: The emperor, mutilated and exiled in 695, regains his throne with Tervel's army and rewards him with the title of Caesar.

title: Umayyad conquest of Iberia
summary: Tariq ibn Ziyad defeats King Roderic, and the Visigothic Kingdom collapses within a few years.

title: Second Arab siege of Constantinople
summary: Leo III, Greek fire, a harsh winter and Bulgar attacks destroy the huge Umayyad army and fleet (717–718).

title: Iconoclasm begins
summary: Leo III moves against icon veneration (726–730), beginning a century-long dispute over religious images.

title: Battle of Tours (Poitiers)
summary: Charles Martel's Franks defeat an Umayyad raid led by Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi.

title: Battle of Akroinon
summary: Leo III and Constantine V crush a major Arab invasion of Anatolia.

title: Abbasid revolution
summary: The Umayyads are defeated at the Battle of the Zab and massacred. A surviving prince flees to Córdoba.

sources.cite: al-Tabari, History of Prophets and Kings

title: Battle of Talas
summary: An Abbasid army defeats Tang forces in Central Asia, checking Chinese expansion westward.

sources.cite: Du Huan, Jingxing ji (a Tang prisoner's account)

title: Lombards take Ravenna
summary: The Exarchate of Ravenna falls; the Pope turns to the Franks for protection.

sources.cite: Liber Pontificalis, Life of Stephen II

title: Iconoclast Council of Hieria
summary: Constantine V's council formally condemns icons.

sources.cite: Horos of Hieria (preserved in the Acts of Nicaea II)

title: An Lushan rebellion
summary: A frontier general's revolt (755–763) devastates Tang China; Uyghur cavalry help restore the dynasty.

sources.cite: Du Fu's poems on the rebellion

title: Baghdad founded
summary: Caliph al-Mansur builds his circular 'City of Peace' on the Tigris.

title: Second Council of Nicaea
summary: Convened under Empress Irene, it restores the veneration of icons.

sources.cite: Acts of the Second Council of Nicaea

title: Viking raid on Lindisfarne
summary: Norse raiders sack the island monastery, conventionally the start of the Viking Age.

sources.cite: Alcuin of York, letter to King Æthelred of Northumbria

title: Irene rules as sole empress
summary: Irene blinds her son Constantine VI and reigns in her own right, which the West treats as a vacant throne when crowning Charlemagne.

title: Charlemagne crowned emperor
summary: Pope Leo III crowns the Frankish king Emperor of the Romans on Christmas Day in St Peter's.

sources.cite: Royal Frankish Annals, s.a. 801 (new year counted from Christmas)

title: Jayavarman II proclaimed universal monarch
summary: A consecration on Phnom Kulen declares Khmer independence from 'Java' and founds the Angkorian empire.

title: Battle of Pliska
summary: Krum traps and kills Emperor Nikephoros I in a mountain pass and makes a drinking cup from his skull.

title: Battle of Versinikia
summary: Krum routs Michael I, leading to Leo V's coup; Krum besieges Constantinople but dies in 814.

title: Andalusi exiles seize Crete
summary: Refugees from Córdoba found an emirate on Crete that raids the Aegean for 140 years.

title: Aghlabid conquest of Sicily begins
summary: Arab forces land at Mazara; Syracuse falls in 878 and the last Byzantine fortress in 902.

title: Sack of Amorium
summary: Caliph al-Mu'tasim destroys the home city of the reigning Amorian dynasty in revenge for Theophilos's raids.

title: Treaty of Verdun
summary: Charlemagne's grandsons divide the empire in three, foreshadowing France and Germany.

title: Triumph of Orthodoxy
summary: Empress Theodora restores icons for good, ending Iconoclasm.

title: First Rus' attack on Constantinople
summary: A Rus' fleet appears without warning and ravages the suburbs while the emperor is away.

title: Cyril and Methodius go to Moravia
summary: The brothers from Thessalonica create the Glagolitic alphabet and a Slavonic liturgy.

sources.cite: Life of Constantine-Cyril; Life of Methodius

title: Bulgaria converts to Christianity
summary: Boris I is baptized with Michael III as godfather, taking the name Michael.

sources.cite: Responses of Pope Nicholas I to the Bulgarians (866)

title: Basil I founds the Macedonian dynasty
summary: Michael III's favourite has him murdered and takes the throne; the dynasty rules for nearly two centuries.

title: Byzantium recovers Bari
summary: The city becomes the capital of Byzantine southern Italy until 1071.

title: Oleg makes Kiev his capital
summary: The Varangian prince Oleg seizes Kiev and unites it with Novgorod. The date is the chronicle's.

title: Fall of the Tang dynasty
summary: The warlord Zhu Wen deposes the last Tang emperor, opening the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period.

sources.cite: Ouyang Xiu, New History of the Five Dynasties

title: Battle of Achelous
summary: Symeon of Bulgaria annihilates a Byzantine army near Anchialos, one of the worst defeats in Byzantine history.

sources.cite: Leo the Deacon (later account); Theophanes Continuatus 6

title: Romanos Lekapenos takes power
summary: The admiral becomes co-emperor and effective ruler for the young Constantine VII.

title: Æthelstan unifies England
summary: After taking York, Æthelstan receives the submission of northern rulers at Eamont and becomes the first king of all England.

title: Abd al-Rahman III proclaims the Caliphate of Córdoba
summary: The Umayyad ruler of al-Andalus claims the caliphal title.

title: Igor's Rus' fleet burned
summary: Greek fire destroys the Rus' fleet off the Bosporus; a trade treaty follows in 944.

title: Battle of Lechfeld
summary: Otto I defeats the Magyars near Augsburg, ending their raids into western Europe.

sources.cite: Gerhard, Life of Ulrich of Augsburg

title: Princess Olga visits Constantinople
summary: The regent of Kiev is received at court and baptized; Constantine VII records the ceremony.

title: Song dynasty founded
summary: The general Zhao Kuangyin is proclaimed emperor by his troops at Chenqiao and makes Kaifeng his capital.

title: Nikephoros Phokas reconquers Crete
summary: After a winter siege of Chandax, the Arab emirate of Crete is destroyed.

sources.cite: Theodosios the Deacon, The Capture of Crete

title: Otto I crowned emperor
summary: The German king is crowned in Rome, and the Holy Roman Empire begins.

sources.cite: Liudprand of Cremona, Liber de Ottone rege

title: Sviatoslav destroys the Khazar Khaganate
summary: The Rus' prince sacks Sarkel and Atil, ending Khazar power on the steppe.

title: Baptism of Mieszko I of Poland
summary: Conventionally the birth of the Polish state.

title: Byzantium retakes Antioch
summary: The city returns to Byzantine rule after more than 330 years. Nikephoros II is murdered the same year.

title: Fatimids found Cairo
summary: The Fatimid general Jawhar conquers Egypt and lays out a new royal city.

title: Siege of Dorostolon
summary: John Tzimiskes besieges Sviatoslav of Kiev and forces him out of Bulgaria, which Byzantium then annexes in the east.

title: Christianization of Kievan Rus'
summary: Vladimir the Great is baptized and marries a Byzantine princess, tying Rus' to Orthodox Christianity.

title: Varangian Guard founded
summary: 6,000 Rus' warriors sent by Vladimir help Basil II defeat rebels; they become the emperor's Norse bodyguard.

title: Stephen I crowned king of Hungary
summary: The Árpád prince is crowned with a crown sent by the pope.

title: Battle of Kleidion
summary: Basil II traps Tsar Samuel's army; the blinding of thousands of prisoners is said to have killed Samuel from shock.

title: Basil II completes the conquest of Bulgaria
summary: Ohrid surrenders and the First Bulgarian Empire becomes Byzantine provinces.

title: Norse at L'Anse aux Meadows
summary: Tree rings show Norse visitors cut wood in Newfoundland in 1021, the earliest securely dated European presence in the Americas.

sources.cite: Kuitems et al., 'Evidence for European presence in the Americas in AD 1021', Nature (2021)
Saga of the Greenlanders; Saga of Erik the Red

title: Death of Basil II
summary: The empire is at its medieval peak from Armenia to southern Italy, but Basil leaves no heir.

title: Chola raid on Srivijaya
summary: Rajendra I's fleet sacks Srivijaya's ports across the Strait of Malacca.

title: Mahmud of Ghazni raids Somnath
summary: The sultan sacks the famous Hindu temple on the Gujarat coast.

title: Byzantium annexes Ani
summary: The Bagratid Armenian kingdom is absorbed, removing a buffer just before the Seljuks arrive.

title: Cahokia's 'Big Bang'
summary: Cahokia is rapidly rebuilt as a planned city around Monks Mound, with perhaps 10,000–20,000 people.

sources.cite: Monks Mound and Grand Plaza excavations
T. R. Pauketat, Cahokia: Ancient America's Great City on the Mississippi (2009)

title: East–West Schism
summary: Papal legates and Patriarch Michael Keroularios excommunicate each other, conventionally marking the split of Catholic and Orthodox churches.

sources.cite: Bull of excommunication by Cardinal Humbert

title: Tughril Beg enters Baghdad
summary: The Seljuk leader becomes protector of the Abbasid caliph and takes the title of sultan.

title: Battle of Hastings
summary: William of Normandy defeats Harold II. The Norman Conquest remakes England's ruling class and language.

title: Battle of Manzikert
summary: The Seljuk sultan Alp Arslan captures Emperor Romanos IV, opening Anatolia to Turkish settlement.

title: Normans take Bari
summary: Robert Guiscard captures the last Byzantine stronghold in Italy in the same year as Manzikert.

sources.cite: William of Apulia, Deeds of Robert Guiscard 2

title: Sultanate of Rum founded
summary: Suleiman ibn Qutalmish establishes a Seljuk state in Anatolia, briefly ruling from Nicaea.

title: Alexios I Komnenos seizes power
summary: The general takes Constantinople and begins the Komnenian restoration.

title: Battle of Dyrrhachium
summary: Robert Guiscard defeats Alexios, whose Varangian Guard is cut to pieces.

title: Alexios grants Venice trading privileges
summary: In return for naval help against the Normans, Venice gets tax-free trade throughout the empire.

title: Domesday survey
summary: William I orders a census of land and livestock across England, the most complete record of a medieval kingdom.

title: Battle of Levounion
summary: Alexios and his Cuman allies annihilate the Pecheneg horde in Thrace.

title: Urban II preaches the Crusade
summary: Answering Alexios's appeal for mercenaries, the pope calls for an armed pilgrimage to Jerusalem.

title: Crusaders and Byzantines take Nicaea
summary: The city surrenders to Alexios rather than the crusaders, souring relations.

title: Crusaders take Antioch
summary: Bohemond keeps the city for himself, breaking the crusaders' oaths to Alexios.

title: Crusaders capture Jerusalem
summary: The First Crusade takes Jerusalem and massacres its inhabitants, founding the crusader states.

title: Treaty of Devol
summary: Defeated by Alexios, Bohemond swears to hold Antioch as a Byzantine vassal.

title: Zengi takes Edessa
summary: The fall of the first crusader state triggers the Second Crusade.

title: Murder of Thomas Becket
summary: Four knights of Henry II kill the archbishop in Canterbury Cathedral.

sources.cite: Edward Grim, Life of St Thomas (Grim was wounded defending him)

title: Battle of Myriokephalon
summary: Manuel I's army is ambushed by Kilij Arslan II, ending hopes of reconquering inner Anatolia.

sources.cite: Manuel's letter to Henry II, in Roger of Howden

title: Massacre of the Latins
summary: A mob in Constantinople kills or enslaves thousands of Italian residents as Andronikos I takes power.

title: Bulgarian revolt of Peter and Asen
summary: A tax revolt against Isaac II Angelos founds the Second Bulgarian Empire.

title: Battle of Hattin
summary: Saladin destroys the army of the Kingdom of Jerusalem and takes the city three months later.

title: Richard I takes Cyprus
summary: On the way to the Third Crusade, Richard seizes the island from the rebel Byzantine ruler Isaac Komnenos.

sources.cite: Ambroise, Estoire de la guerre sainte

title: Fourth Crusade sacks Constantinople
summary: Diverted by Venetian debts and a Byzantine pretender, the crusaders storm the city and partition the empire.

title: Empire of Trebizond founded
summary: Alexios and David Komnenos take Trebizond with Georgian troops sent by Queen Tamar.

title: Battle of Adrianople
summary: Kaloyan of Bulgaria and his Cuman allies crush the crusaders and capture Emperor Baldwin I.

title: Temüjin proclaimed Chinggis Khan
summary: A great assembly at the source of the Onon River makes Temüjin ruler of all the steppe peoples.

sources.cite: The Secret History of the Mongols §202

title: Theodore Laskaris crowned at Nicaea
summary: The patriarch in exile crowns Theodore emperor, making Nicaea the main Byzantine government in exile.

title: Magna Carta sealed
summary: At Runnymede, rebel barons force King John to accept limits on royal power.

sources.cite: Magna Carta (1215; British Library Cotton MS Augustus II.106)

title: Mongols take Zhongdu (Beijing)
summary: The Jin dynasty's capital falls after a long siege.

title: Battle of Klokotnitsa
summary: Ivan Asen II defeats and captures Theodore of Epirus, ending Epirote hopes of retaking Constantinople.

title: Battle of Kirina: Mali founded
summary: Sundiata Keita defeats Sumanguru of Sosso and founds the Mali Empire. The date is traditional.

title: Mongols sack Kiev
summary: Batu's army storms Kiev, ending Kievan Rus'. The Rus' principalities become Golden Horde tributaries.

sources.cite: Giovanni da Pian del Carpine, Ystoria Mongalorum (passed through in 1246)

title: Mongols at Legnica and Mohi
summary: Two Mongol armies crush Polish and Hungarian forces before withdrawing on news of Ögedei's death.

sources.cite: Roger of Torre Maggiore, Carmen Miserabile

title: Battle of Köse Dağ
summary: The Mongols defeat the Sultanate of Rum, which becomes a vassal; Anatolia fragments into Turkish beyliks.

title: Mongols sack Baghdad
summary: Hülegü takes the city and executes Caliph al-Musta'sim, ending the Abbasid Caliphate in Baghdad.

title: Battle of Pelagonia
summary: Michael VIII's forces defeat Epirus and its Latin allies, clearing the way to Constantinople.

title: Battle of Ain Jalut
summary: The Mamluks of Egypt defeat a Mongol army, halting their advance into Africa.

title: Byzantines recapture Constantinople
summary: A small Nicaean force under Alexios Strategopoulos slips into the city; Michael VIII enters in triumph.

title: Union of Lyon
summary: Michael VIII submits the Church to Rome to head off Charles of Anjou's invasion; the union is hated at home.

sources.cite: Acts of the Second Council of Lyon

title: Battle of Yamen: end of the Song
summary: Kublai Khan's Yuan fleet destroys the last Song loyalists. China is united under Mongol rule.

title: Sicilian Vespers
summary: A revolt in Palermo, backed by Byzantine gold and Aragon, destroys Charles of Anjou's plan to invade Byzantium.

title: Battle of Bạch Đằng
summary: Trần Hưng Đạo destroys a Yuan fleet with stakes set in the river bed, ending Mongol invasions.

sources.cite: Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư

title: Fall of Acre
summary: The Mamluks take the last major crusader city.

title: Osman founds the Ottoman state
summary: A Turkish frontier lord in Bithynia begins the dynasty that bears his name. The traditional date is approximate.

title: Battle of Bapheus
summary: Osman defeats a Byzantine force near Nicomedia, the first Ottoman victory over the empire.

title: Catalan Company turns on Byzantium
summary: Mercenaries hired against the Turks ravage Thrace after their leader Roger de Flor is murdered.

title: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage passes through Cairo
summary: The Mali emperor spends so much gold in Cairo that local writers said its value dropped for years.

title: Tenochtitlan founded
summary: The Mexica settle an island in Lake Texcoco where, by tradition, they saw an eagle on a cactus.

title: Ottomans take Bursa
summary: Prusa surrenders to Orhan after a long blockade and becomes the first Ottoman capital.

title: Byzantine civil war of 1341–1347
summary: John Kantakouzenos fights the regency of John V; both sides hire Serbs and Turks, ruining the empire.

title: Stefan Dušan crowned emperor
summary: At Skopje the Serbian ruler takes the title 'Emperor of the Serbs and Greeks'.

title: Battle of Crécy
summary: English longbowmen destroy the French knights early in the Hundred Years' War.

sources.cite: Edward III's newsletter from the campaign

title: Black Death reaches Europe
summary: Plague arrives at Messina in Sicily via Genoese galleys from the Black Sea and kills perhaps a third to a half of Europeans.

sources.cite: Gabriele de' Mussis, Historia de Morbo
Yersinia pestis ancient DNA studies (e.g., Spyrou et al., Nature 2022)

title: Black Death reaches Constantinople
summary: The plague kills Kantakouzenos's son Andronikos and much of the city.

title: Ottomans occupy Gallipoli
summary: After an earthquake wrecks the town's walls, Orhan's son Suleiman crosses into Europe and stays.

title: Ming dynasty founded
summary: Zhu Yuanzhang proclaims the Ming at Nanjing. The Yuan court flees Beijing for Mongolia.

title: Battle of the Maritsa
summary: The Ottomans destroy a Serbian army; Byzantium and Bulgaria soon become Ottoman vassals.

title: Battle of Kosovo
summary: Murad I and Prince Lazar are both killed; Serbia becomes an Ottoman vassal.

sources.cite: Konstantin of Kostenets, Life of Despot Stefan

title: Ottomans take Tarnovo
summary: Bayezid I captures the Bulgarian capital; the last Bulgarian state falls by 1396.

sources.cite: Gregory Tsamblak, Eulogy of Patriarch Euthymius

title: Battle of Nicopolis
summary: A crusade led by Sigismund of Hungary and French knights is crushed by Bayezid I.

sources.cite: Johann Schiltberger, Bondage and Travels (a captive)

title: Timur sacks Delhi
summary: Timur's army plunders Delhi and kills much of its population.

title: Manuel II tours western Europe
summary: The emperor visits Paris and London seeking aid while Constantinople is blockaded.

title: Battle of Ankara
summary: Timur defeats and captures Sultan Bayezid I, nearly destroying the Ottoman state.

sources.cite: Ruy González de Clavijo, Embassy to Tamerlane

title: Zheng He's first treasure voyage
summary: The first of seven Ming fleets sails into the Indian Ocean. Later voyages reach East Africa.

title: Battle of Grunwald
summary: Poland and Lithuania crush the Teutonic Order.

title: Battle of Agincourt
summary: Henry V's outnumbered army defeats the French.

sources.cite: Gesta Henrici Quinti (by a chaplain in Henry's army)
Jean de Waurin, Chronicles (fought on the French side)

title: Aztec Triple Alliance formed
summary: Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan overthrow Azcapotzalco and begin building a tributary empire.

sources.cite: Diego Durán, History of the Indies of New Spain

title: Joan of Arc relieves Orléans
summary: The siege is lifted, and Charles VII is crowned at Reims.

sources.cite: Trial of Condemnation (1431) and Trial of Rehabilitation testimonies (1455–56)

title: Ottomans take Thessalonica
summary: Murad II storms the city, which Venice had held since 1423.

sources.cite: John Anagnostes, Account of the Fall of Thessalonica

title: Ayutthaya sacks Angkor
summary: Siamese forces take Angkor. The Khmer court soon moves south toward Phnom Penh. The traditional date is debated.

sources.cite: Angkor hydraulic decline studies (e.g., Buckley et al., PNAS 2010)

title: Pachacuti begins Inca expansion
summary: After defeating the Chanka, Pachacuti rebuilds Cusco and turns a local kingdom into an empire.

sources.cite: Juan de Betanzos, Suma y narración de los Incas (1551)
Pedro Cieza de León, Crónica del Perú

title: Council of Florence
summary: John VIII agrees to union of the churches in hope of a crusade; it is rejected in Constantinople.

title: Battle of Varna
summary: The last great crusade is destroyed and King Władysław III is killed.

title: Rumeli Hisarı built
summary: Mehmed II builds a fortress on the Bosporus in four months to cut off the city's Black Sea supplies.

title: Fall of Constantinople
summary: Mehmed II breaches the Theodosian Walls with heavy cannon, ending the Roman Empire after some 1,500 years.

sources.cite: Nicolò Barbaro, Diary of the Siege
Kritoboulos, History of Mehmed the Conqueror

title: Gutenberg Bible printed
summary: Movable-type printing in Mainz spreads across Europe within decades.

sources.cite: Letter of Enea Silvio Piccolomini (later Pope Pius II), March 1455, describing the sheets

title: Fall of the Despotate of the Morea
summary: Mehmed II takes Mistras, the last Byzantine-ruled territory in Greece.

title: Fall of Trebizond
summary: The last Byzantine successor state surrenders to Mehmed II.

title: Inca conquer Chimú
summary: Topa Inca's armies take Chan Chan and move its craftsmen to Cusco.

title: Great Stand on the Ugra River
summary: Ivan III faces down Khan Akhmat's army, conventionally ending the 'Tatar yoke' over Muscovy.

sources.cite: Russian chronicles, s.a. 1480 (e.g., Sofia II, Vologda-Perm)

title: Columbus reaches the Caribbean
summary: A Castilian expedition lands in the Bahamas, beginning sustained contact, colonization and the Columbian Exchange. The same year Granada falls.

title: Treaty of Tordesillas
summary: Castile and Portugal divide newly found lands along a meridian 370 leagues west of Cape Verde, the basis of Portuguese Brazil.

sources.cite: Treaty of Tordesillas (Archivo General de Indias; Torre do Tombo)

title: Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut
summary: The first sea voyage from Europe to India, around Africa, begins Portugal's Indian Ocean empire.

sources.cite: Álvaro Velho (attrib.), Roteiro of the first voyage

title: Cabral reaches Brazil
summary: A Portuguese fleet bound for India lands at Porto Seguro.

sources.cite: Pero Vaz de Caminha, letter to King Manuel I (1 May 1500)

title: Ismail I crowned at Tabriz
summary: The Safavid shah proclaims Twelver Shi'ism as the state religion of Iran.

title: Ottomans conquer Mamluk Egypt
summary: Selim I takes Cairo, bringing Egypt, Syria and the Holy Cities of Arabia under Ottoman rule.

sources.cite: Ibn Iyas, Bada'i' al-Zuhur (an eyewitness in Cairo)

title: Luther's Ninety-five Theses
summary: A Wittenberg friar's challenge to the sale of indulgences begins the Protestant Reformation.

sources.cite: Martin Luther, Ninety-five Theses and letter to Archbishop Albrecht (31 October 1517)

title: Cortés lands in Mexico
summary: Cortés founds Veracruz, scuttles his ships and marches inland with Totonac and later Tlaxcalan allies.

sources.cite: Bernal Díaz del Castillo, True History of the Conquest of New Spain

title: Fall of Tenochtitlan
summary: After a 75-day siege, Cortés and his Tlaxcalan allies capture the Mexica capital, already ravaged by smallpox.

sources.cite: Bernal Díaz del Castillo, True History of the Conquest

title: First Battle of Panipat
summary: Babur's guns and cavalry defeat Ibrahim Lodi. The Delhi Sultanate ends and the Mughal Empire begins.

title: Battle of Mohács
summary: Suleiman the Magnificent destroys the Hungarian army; King Louis II dies in the retreat.

sources.cite: István Brodarics, True Account of the Battle

title: Pizarro captures Atahualpa
summary: At Cajamarca a small Spanish force seizes the Inca ruler, who had just won a civil war. He is executed in 1533.

sources.cite: Francisco de Xerez, True Account of the Conquest of Peru (1534)

title: Ivan IV conquers Kazan
summary: The fall of the Kazan Khanate opens the Volga and, beyond it, Siberia to Russian expansion.

title: Battle of Talikota
summary: An alliance of Deccan sultanates defeats Vijayanagara, and its capital is sacked.

title: Spanish Armada defeated
summary: Philip II's invasion fleet is beaten off Gravelines and wrecked on its way home around Scotland and Ireland.

sources.cite: Letters of the Duke of Medina Sidonia and Francisco de Cuéllar's account

title: Battle of Tondibi
summary: A Moroccan expeditionary army with firearms crushes the Songhai, ending the last great Sahel empire.

title: Jamestown founded
summary: The first permanent English colony in North America is founded in Powhatan territory.

title: Champlain founds Quebec
summary: The first permanent settlement of New France.

title: Defenestration of Prague
summary: Bohemian Protestants throw imperial officials from a castle window, starting the Thirty Years' War.

sources.cite: Account of the regent Vilém Slavata (one of the men thrown)

title: Plymouth Colony founded
summary: The Mayflower passengers settle on Wampanoag land and sign the Mayflower Compact.

title: Qing take Beijing
summary: After rebels topple the Ming, Manchu armies enter through the Great Wall and make Beijing the Qing capital.

title: Peace of Westphalia
summary: Treaties at Münster and Osnabrück end the Thirty Years' War and confirm the sovereignty of the Empire's princes.

title: Execution of Charles I
summary: After the civil wars, Parliament tries and beheads the king; England becomes a republic until 1660.

sources.cite: Death warrant of Charles I (Parliamentary Archives)

title: Pueblo Revolt
summary: Pueblo peoples led by Popé drive the Spanish from New Mexico for twelve years.

title: Siege of Vienna
summary: A relief army under Jan III Sobieski routs the Ottomans. The Habsburgs then reconquer Hungary.

sources.cite: Silahdar Fındıklılı Mehmed Ağa, Silahdar Tarihi
Jan III Sobieski, letters to Queen Marie Casimire

title: Acts of Union create Great Britain
summary: The parliaments of England and Scotland merge into a single Kingdom of Great Britain.

sources.cite: Union with Scotland Act 1706; Union with England Act 1707

title: Battle of Poltava
summary: Peter the Great destroys Charles XII's army, ending Sweden's great-power era.

sources.cite: Peter I's letters from the field

title: Peter I proclaims the Russian Empire
summary: After victory over Sweden (Treaty of Nystad), the Senate gives Peter the title Emperor of All Russia.

title: Battle of Plassey
summary: East India Company forces under Robert Clive defeat the Nawab of Bengal, beginning British territorial rule in India.

sources.cite: Robert Clive's dispatches (British Library, India Office Records)

title: Treaty of Paris (1763) and Royal Proclamation
summary: France cedes Canada and lands east of the Mississippi to Britain and Louisiana to Spain. The Proclamation Line reserves the interior for Native nations.

title: Fall of Ayutthaya
summary: Burmese armies destroy the Siamese capital.

title: First Partition of Poland
summary: Russia, Prussia and Austria seize a third of the Commonwealth; by 1795 Poland disappears from the map.

title: Lexington and Concord
summary: The first shots of the American Revolutionary War.

sources.cite: Diary of Lt. John Barker, King's Own Regiment

title: American Declaration of Independence
summary: Thirteen British colonies declare independence. Britain recognizes the United States in 1783.

title: Treaty of Paris recognizes the United States
summary: Britain recognizes U.S. independence with borders from the Atlantic to the Mississippi and from the Great Lakes to Florida. The U.S. state map begins here.

sources.cite: Treaty of Paris (3 September 1783), National Archives

title: French Revolution
summary: The storming of the Bastille and the Declaration of the Rights of Man begin the overthrow of the absolute monarchy.

sources.cite: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen (26 August 1789)

title: Haitian Revolution begins
summary: Enslaved people rise in Saint-Domingue; independence follows in 1804.

title: Louisiana Purchase
summary: The United States buys France's claim to the Mississippi's western basin, roughly doubling its size.

sources.cite: Louisiana Purchase Treaty (30 April 1803), National Archives

title: Napoleon crowned Emperor
summary: Napoleon crowns himself in Notre-Dame.

sources.cite: Memoirs of Madame de Rémusat (attended the court)
Jacques-Louis David, The Coronation of Napoleon (Louvre)

title: Lewis and Clark winter at Fort Mandan
summary: The expedition builds Fort Mandan near the Mandan and Hidatsa villages and meets Sacagawea before heading west.

sources.cite: Journals of Meriwether Lewis and William Clark (1804–1806)

title: Holy Roman Empire dissolved
summary: Facing Napoleon's Confederation of the Rhine, Francis II lays down the imperial crown.

sources.cite: Abdication proclamation of Francis II (6 August 1806)

title: Napoleon's invasion of Russia
summary: The Grande Armée takes Moscow but loses most of its 600,000 men in the retreat.

sources.cite: Armand de Caulaincourt, Memoirs (at Napoleon's side)
Philippe-Paul de Ségur, History of the Expedition to Russia

title: Waterloo and the Congress of Vienna
summary: Napoleon is defeated for the last time, and the Congress of Vienna redraws Europe's borders.

sources.cite: Final Act of the Congress of Vienna (9 June 1815)

title: Mexican independence
summary: The Plan of Iguala and the Treaty of Córdoba end Spanish rule.

sources.cite: Plan of Iguala; Treaty of Córdoba (1821)

title: Brazilian independence
summary: Prince Pedro declares independence by the Ipiranga stream and becomes emperor.

sources.cite: Accounts of Pedro I's companions at Ipiranga

title: Trail of Tears
summary: After the Indian Removal Act (1830), the U.S. Army forces the Cherokee west; thousands die on the march.

sources.cite: Indian Removal Act (1830); Treaty of New Echota (1835)
Diary of Lt. John G. Burnett; missionary Daniel Butrick's journal

title: Revolutions of 1848
summary: Uprisings sweep France, the German states, Austria and Italy; most are suppressed by 1849.

title: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo
summary: Mexico cedes California and the Southwest after losing the U.S.–Mexican War.

title: Indian Rebellion and the end of the Mughals
summary: After the uprising is crushed, Bahadur Shah II is exiled. The Crown takes over India from the East India Company in 1858.

sources.cite: Trial proceedings of Bahadur Shah Zafar (1858)

title: Kingdom of Italy proclaimed
summary: After Garibaldi's conquest of the south, Victor Emmanuel II becomes king of Italy at Turin.

title: American Civil War begins
summary: Confederate guns fire on Fort Sumter in Charleston harbour.

sources.cite: Official Records of the War of the Rebellion

title: Battle of Gettysburg
summary: The Union defeats Lee's invasion of the North; Lincoln's address follows in November.

sources.cite: Frank Haskell, letter on the battle (1863)

title: Surrender at Appomattox
summary: Lee surrenders to Grant; the Thirteenth Amendment abolishes slavery that year.

title: Canadian Confederation
summary: Ontario, Quebec, Nova Scotia and New Brunswick unite as the Dominion of Canada.

title: Alaska Purchase
summary: The United States buys Alaska from Russia for $7.2 million.

title: German Empire proclaimed
summary: After defeating France, Wilhelm I of Prussia is proclaimed German Emperor in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles.

sources.cite: Constitution of the German Empire (16 April 1871)

title: Battle of the Little Bighorn
summary: Lakota, Cheyenne and Arapaho warriors under Sitting Bull and Crazy Horse defeat Custer's 7th Cavalry.

sources.cite: Accounts of Lakota and Cheyenne participants collected by Walter Camp and others

title: Berlin Conference
summary: European powers set rules for claiming African territory, accelerating the 'Scramble for Africa'.

sources.cite: General Act of the Berlin Conference (26 February 1885)

title: North and South Dakota become states
summary: Dakota Territory is divided and admitted as two states under the Enabling Act of 1889.

title: Wounded Knee Massacre
summary: U.S. troops kill some 250–300 Lakota men, women and children.

sources.cite: Testimony of survivors, and Black Elk Speaks (1932)

title: British sack of Benin City
summary: A punitive expedition burns the city and loots the Benin Bronzes.

sources.cite: R. H. Bacon, Benin: The City of Blood (1897)

title: Last Qing emperor abdicates
summary: The Xinhai Revolution, begun at Wuchang in 1911, ends more than two thousand years of imperial rule in China.

sources.cite: Edict of abdication of the Xuantong Emperor (12 February 1912)

title: First World War begins
summary: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo triggers a war that destroys four empires.

title: Panama Canal opens
summary: The canal links the Atlantic and Pacific.

title: Russian Revolutions
summary: The tsar abdicates in March. In November the Bolsheviks seize power in Petrograd.

sources.cite: Manifesto of Nicholas II's abdication (15 March 1917)

title: Treaty of Versailles
summary: The peace after the First World War redraws Europe's borders and creates new states from the fallen empires.

sources.cite: Harold Nicolson, Peacemaking 1919 (diary of a delegate)

title: Ottoman sultanate abolished
summary: The Grand National Assembly in Ankara abolishes the sultanate. The Republic of Turkey is proclaimed in 1923.

sources.cite: Resolution of the Grand National Assembly (1 November 1922)

title: Soviet Union founded
summary: Russia, Ukraine, Belarus and the Transcaucasian republics form the USSR.

sources.cite: Treaty on the Creation of the USSR (30 December 1922)

title: Germany invades Poland
summary: The Second World War begins in Europe; the Soviet Union invades from the east on 17 September.

title: End of the Second World War; UN founded
summary: Germany and Japan surrender. Fifty nations sign the UN Charter in San Francisco.

sources.cite: Charter of the United Nations (26 June 1945)

title: Independence and partition of India
summary: India and Pakistan become independent amid partition violence that displaced millions.

title: People's Republic of China proclaimed
summary: After the civil war, Mao Zedong proclaims the PRC in Beijing. The Republic of China government retreats to Taiwan.

sources.cite: Proclamation of the Central People's Government (1 October 1949)

title: Treaty of Rome
summary: Six states found the European Economic Community, forerunner of the European Union.

sources.cite: Treaty establishing the European Economic Community (1957)

title: The Year of Africa
summary: Seventeen African states gain independence in a single year as European empires dissolve.

title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
